concept.name: Operational risk
concept.definition: The risk of loss resulting from inadequate or failed internal processes, people, and systems or from external events — including fraud, execution errors, outages, and legal risk. It is the Basel definition used for bank capital purposes, and the risk is inherent in all products, activities, processes, and systems.
concept.intuition: It is the risk that something inside the machine — or an outside event hitting the machine — breaks: the rogue trade, the failed settlement, the system outage, the fat-finger order.
concept.mechanics: Managed through governance and control frameworks, risk and control self-assessments, loss-event data collection, and scenario analysis; capitalized under the Basel standardized approach for operational risk. For trading operations it includes order-entry errors, model implementation bugs, and venue or broker failures.
concept.formula: No canonical concept-level formula; Basel capital uses a business-indicator-based standardized approach (business indicator component times internal loss multiplier).
concept.failure_modes: Operational losses are fat-tailed and event-driven, so historical loss data understates the worst cases; controls themselves fail under stress (the alert that never fires, the reconciliation nobody reads), and automation converts small errors into large, fast ones.
concept.misconceptions: Operational risk is not a vague residual category — it has a precise regulatory definition — and sophisticated technology raises rather than lowers its stakes, because failures then scale at machine speed.
concept.example: A misconfigured order router sending duplicated orders, or a clearing outage preventing end-of-day settlement, produces operational-risk losses unrelated to any market view.

citations.source: BCBS: Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk
